question.text: In Series XIX-A fund due diligence, the manager's "value creation" in portfolio companies refers PRIMARILY to:

answer.text: Excess return generated only by buying low and selling high
The return generated by the fund's back-office team

Active management and operational improvements in portfolio companies — for example restructuring, strategic repositioning, leveraging, and other operational improvements demonstrated through case studies
The alpha generated by algorithmic trading operations

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook frames fund due diligence around active management, value-creation strategy, and an assessment of manager expertise. Its DD prompts explicitly ask about restructuring, strategic repositioning, leveraging, operational improvements, and case studies of value creation in portfolio companies. This is the workbook's definition of how AIF managers add value. The Trap: Pure entry/exit timing, back-office work, and algorithmic trading are not the workbook's value-creation prompts. Note: The non-workbook term "operational alpha" was replaced with workbook language — "value creation" through operational improvements in portfolio companies. Cross-Exam and Pro-Tip paragraphs were removed.
